plot: At 5:59 a.m. in the kitchen the same minute keeps repeating and a flour sack buries the bros every loop; only Crispy remembers, he and Bup test hiding and catching, then notice the clock jumps back whenever sleepwalking Pim whispers 'one more minute', so Pim, held by his friends, wishes for a brave good morning, time moves on, and the oven clock starts a 13-minute countdown no one wished for.

script.title: How We Escaped the Minute That Wouldn't End

beats.say: RUN! The flour sack is falling! Everybody off the counter, right now!
Ahh! Not again! Wait... why did I just say again?
Poof. A white cloud swallows the kitchen. Then the clock ticks back to five fifty-nine, and everything starts over.
RUN! The flour sack is fall... hold on. I have said this exact sentence before.
Eleven times, loaf. You have shouted it eleven times.
Eleven?! Then why does nobody else remember it?
I was burnt so long ago that time slides off me like grease. I remember every single loop.
Good morning, everyone! Did anyone else dream about being covered in flour?
Five friends sharing one flour dream is statistically impossible. Unless... the dream is real.
It is real. The same minute keeps happening. And it happens again in thirty seconds.
Loop twelve. New idea. Everybody hides under the cutting board!
Under the board? But it's d-d-dark under the board!
Pim, sweetheart, it's either dark or floury. Pick one.
They hide. The sack misses the counter... and lands right on the cutting board. Flat. Floury. Again.
Hiding never works. The minute always finds you.
Then we stop the sack itself. Zeek, can you catch it?
With a spaghetti net and a spoon spring! My calculations need twenty seconds.
The net is ready! Nineteen seconds left. Wait, why is the clock already—
Loop fourteen. Fifteen. Twenty. By loop thirty, there is not one clean crumb left on the counter.
Crispy, this is not a flour problem. Something is pushing that clock backwards.
Finally. Now stop watching the sack. Watch the clock.
The minute hand jumps back right when... somebody yawns.
Listen.
Mmm... one more minute... please, clock... just one more minute...
Pim is asleep standing up! He's been whispering to the clock this whole time!
Fascinating! A sleepy wish so strong that it rewinds a whole kitchen!
I'm n-n-not asleep! I'm resting my eyes very loudly!
Pim, every time you wish for one more minute, thirty pounds of flour lands on us.
But mornings are scary. In the morning the stove wakes up and starts hissing.
Then don't wish for more night, little bean. Wish for a good morning.
And we'll stand right next to you when the stove wakes up. All of us. Promise.
Everybody, hold hands. Or crusts. Or corners. Whatever we've got.
Clock! I wish for a good morning! A brave one! With my friends!
The sack falls... and misses everyone by one crumb. The clock clicks forward. Six o'clock.
We're out! Real time! Glorious, normal, boring time!
Good job, Pim. Next time you're scared, just ask us for a hug.
Quiet. Count the ticks.
Across the kitchen, the oven clock blinks on by itself. It is not counting forward. It is counting down.
Thirteen minutes. And this time, nobody here made a wish.
